page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The server is equipped with a 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra processor configured with 1 physical core, 1 vCPU, and 1 thread per core. Compute resources are provided via dedicated CPU allocation, avoiding the shared-thread performance fluctuations common in burstable environments.

System memory totals 4.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. This instance configuration does not include local storage disks, requiring remote block storage for operating system images and persistent application data. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included. Network provisioning incorporates one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the minimal single-core footprint offers a dedicated baseline without the overhead of unused multi-core capacity. The dedicated 3.0 GHz ARM64 core provides predictable single-threaded execution, although compute-heavy parallel tasks and storage-intensive applications will be constrained by the single-core topology and lack of local NVMe storage.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-4 is appropriate for lightweight web serving, low-traffic microservices, software testing on 64-bit ARM environments, small CI/CD tasks, and basic background utility scripts.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-4 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 1 vCPU and 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture, it features a 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra processor allocated as a dedicated physical core with a single thread per core. The server configuration includes no local storage drives, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistence, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With a fully dedicated CPU core operating at a fixed 3.0 GHz frequency, it eliminates noisy-neighbor issues common in shared-thread virtual environments, providing dependable compute cycles. Qualitatively, this configuration delivers resource-dense efficiency for modest computing demands. Suitable workloads include lightweight web servers, containerized microservices, CI/CD build agents, and ARM64 application development or testing environments.
